translations.text: For many have set their hand to write down a narrative, for the full assurance of faith, of the matters accomplished among us,
just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word,
it seemed right to me also, who have followed all things truly from the beginning, to write to you in order, O valiant lover of God,
so that you may know the reverence of those words concerning which you have been taught.

In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest whose name was Zechariah, following the daily service of Abijah, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
And both of them were righteous before God, and they walked blameless in all the commandments of the righteousness of the Lord.
And they had no child, for Elizabeth was barren, and both of them were advanced in their days.
And it happened, while he was serving as priest in the order of his daily service before God,
According to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him to burn incense, and he entered the temple of the Lord.
And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the burning of incense.
And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.
And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
The angel said to him: Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your petitions have been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
And he will be joy and gladness to you, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before the Lord, and he shall drink no wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
And many of the sons of Israel he will turn to the Lord their God.

And he himself will go out ahead, before him, in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children and the disobedient to the mind of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.
And Zechariah said to the angel: How shall I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in her days.
The angel answered and said: I am Gabriel, who stand before the face of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
And you will be silent and unable to speak until the day that this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time.
And the people stood waiting for Zechariah, and they marveled at his delay in the temple.
And when he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen some vision in the temple; and he kept making signs to them and remained mute.
And it came to pass, when the days of his service were completed, that he went away to his house.
And after these days his wife conceived, and she hid herself for five months, saying,
Thus has the Lord done to me in these days, in which he looked upon me to take away my reproach among men.
And in the sixth month an angel was sent from God to a city of Galilee whose name was Nazareth,
to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house and tribe of David, and the name of the virgin was Mary.
And the angel came in to her and said to her: "Rejoice, favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women."
But when she saw, she was troubled at his word and pondered: What kind of greeting is this?
And the angel said to her: Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found grace before God.
And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.
He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David, his father,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end."
Mary said to the angel: How will this be, for I do not know a man?
The angel answered and said to her: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore also the one who is born will be called holy, the Son of God.
And behold, Elizabeth too, your kinswoman, she also has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
For no word is impossible before God.
Mary said to him: "Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word!" And the angel departed from her.
And in those days Mary arose and went quickly toward the hill country, to a city of Judah.
And she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
And it came to pass, when Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, that the child leapt in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
and cried out with a loud voice and said: "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
And from where does this come to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For behold, as soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, this child leapt for joy in my womb.
And blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things spoken to her by the Lord."
And Mary said: "My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
For he has looked upon the lowliness of his handmaid; behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed;
For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name,
and his mercy is from generation to generation upon those who fear him.
He has acted with the strength of his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thought of their hearts;
he has cast down the mighty from thrones and has exalted the lowly;
he has filled the hungry with good things and has scattered the rich empty-handed;
he has helped Israel, his servant, in remembrance of his mercy,
as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his descendants forever.
And Mary stayed with her three months and went away to her own home.
Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
And her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.
And it came to pass on the eighth day that they came to circumcise the child, and they would have called him by the name of his father, Zechariah.
And his mother answered and said: "No, but let him be called John."
And they said to her: "There is no one among your kindred who is called by that name."
And they made signs to his father, as to what he wished to name him.
And he asked for a tablet and wrote, saying: "John is his name." And all marveled at this.
And immediately his mouth and his tongue were opened, and he spoke and blessed God.
And great fear came upon all who dwelt around them; and throughout all the hill country of Judea all these words were talked about.
And those who heard this laid it up in their hearts and said: "What then will this child be?" And the hand of the Lord was upon that child.
And Zechariah, his father, was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked upon and brought about the redemption of his people;
he has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David, his servant;
As he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old:
deliverance from our enemies and from the hands of all who hate us;
to show mercy to our fathers, to remember his holy covenant;
the oath that he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that, delivered from the hands of our enemies, without fear
to serve him in worthiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
And you, child, shall be called a prophet of the Most High, for you shall go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give knowledge of salvation to his people through the forgiveness of our sins,
through the mercy and compassion of our God, by which the one rising from on high has looked upon us,
to appear to those who sit in darkness and the shadows of death, and to guide our feet in the way of peace.
And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the time of his appearing to Israel.
And it came to pass in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be registered.
This first registration took place during the governorship of Quirinius in Syria.
And all went to be registered, each one to his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and tribe of David,
to be registered with Mary, who was betrothed to him, and she was pregnant.
And it came to pass, while they were there, that the days of her giving birth were fulfilled.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son, and she wrapped him in swaddling cloth and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging.
And there were shepherds in that same region, staying in the fields and keeping the night watch over their flock.
And an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone upon them, and they were afraid with great fear.
And the angel of the Lord said to them: Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy, which shall be for all the people:
for to you has been born a Savior, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.
And this shall be a sign for you: you will find the child wrapped and lying in a manger.
And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the hosts of heaven, praising God and saying:
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, and among men goodwill.

And it came to pass, when the angels had gone up into heaven, that the shepherds said to one another: Let us go over as far as Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened to us, which the Lord has made known to us.
And they came quickly and found Mary and Joseph and the child lying in the manger.
And when they saw it, they understood the word that had been spoken to them about the child.
And those who heard were amazed at the word of the shepherds to them.
But Mary kept all these words and laid them up in her heart.
And the shepherds turned back and departed, glorifying and blessing God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.
And when the eight days of his circumcision were completed, they called his name Jesus, the name he had been called by the angel before he came to be in his mother's womb.
And when the days of their purification were completed according to the law of Moses, they brought the child up to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord,
as it is written in the law of the Lord: Every child that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord;
and to give an offering, as it is said in the law of the Lord: "two turtledoves, or two young pigeons."
And there was a man there in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. And this man was righteous and fearing the Lord, and he was waiting for the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
And it had been made known to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he should see the Anointed of the Lord.
And he came by the Holy Spirit to the temple of the Lord. And when the child Jesus was brought in by his father and mother, so that they might do for him according to the custom of the law,
he took him up in his arms and blessed God and said:
Now release your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace,
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared before the face of all the people,
a light to shine forth upon the Gentiles and the glory of your people Israel.
And his father and mother were amazed at those words about him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother: Behold, this one stands for the fall and the rising of many in Israel, and as a sign for those who speak against him.
And a sword will pass through your own soul too, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."
And there was Anna the prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in many days and had lived with her husband seven years from her virginity.
And she was a widow of about eighty-four years, who did not depart from the temple, with fasting and supplication and service night and day.
And at that same time she arrived and gave thanks to God and spoke about him to all those who were waiting for the redemption of Israel.
And when they had completed everything for him according to the law, they returned and went to Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth.
And the child Jesus grew and became strong in spirit, and was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
And his father and mother would go up year by year to Jerusalem for the feast of Passover, which is the feast of the Passion.
And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem for the feast, as they were accustomed.
And they completed those days, and as they were leaving, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and his father and mother did not know it,
supposing that he was with the fellow travellers. And they went a day's journey and looked for him among their kinsfolk and acquaintances,
and they did not find him. And they returned to Jerusalem and were looking for him.
And it came to pass that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, and he was listening to them and questioning them.
All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
And they saw him and were amazed. And his mother said to him: Son, why have you done this to us? Behold, your father and I are in distress and are looking for you.
And he said to them: Why were you looking for me? Do you not know that I must be with my Father?
And they did not understand the word that he spoke to them.
And he went with them and came to Nazareth and was obedient to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart.
And Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature and in grace before God and people.

In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar, when Pilate the Pontian was governing in Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother was tetrarch of Ituraea and the country of Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
And he came into all the country of the Jordan and preached the baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
As it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah, which says: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the ways of the Lord and make his paths straight.
Every ravine shall be filled up, and all mountains and hills shall be brought low; and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough a smooth road.
And all flesh shall see the salvation of God."
And he said to the crowds who went out to him to be baptized by him: "You offspring of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come?

Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance, and do not suppose and say in your hearts: We have Abraham as our father. For I tell you that God is able to raise up offspring for Abraham from these stones.
For even now the axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree that does not bring forth good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
And the crowds asked him, saying, "What then shall we do?"
He answered and said to them: Whoever has two garments, let him give to the one who has none; and whoever has food, let him do likewise.
Tax collectors also came to him to be baptized, and they said to him, "Teacher, what shall we do?"
But he said to them: Do nothing beyond what has been appointed for you.
Those enrolled as soldiers also asked him and said: And what shall we do? And he said to them: Do not oppress anyone, nor accuse anyone falsely, and let your wages be enough for you.
And as the people were waiting, and all were deliberating in their hearts about John, whether he might perhaps be the Christ,
he answered them all, saying: I baptize you with water, but one mightier than I is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hands, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.
And with many other things as well he exhorted the people and proclaimed the good news to them.
But Herod, the ruler of four dominions, because he reproved him concerning Herodias, the wife of his brother, and concerning all the evil that Herod had done,
added this as well on top of all of it, and shut John up in prison.
And it happened, at the baptism of all the people, that Jesus too was baptized and was praying; the heavens were opened,
and the Holy Spirit came down upon him in bodily form, like a dove; and a voice came from heaven and said: "You are my beloved Son; I am well pleased with you."
And Jesus himself was just beginning to be in his thirtieth year, being, as was supposed, the son of Joseph, of Jacob, of Eli,
of Matthan, of Levi, of Melchi, of Janna, of Joseph,
son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Nahum, son of Esli, son of Naggai,
of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semein, of Joseph, of Judah,
of Joanan, of Rhesa, of Zerubbabel, of Shealtiel, of Neri,
of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
of Joshua, of Eliezer, of Joram, of Matthat, of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim,
son of Melea, son of Menna, son of Mattatha, son of Nathan, son of David,
of Jesse, of Obed, of Boaz, of Salmon, of Nahshon,
the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
of Jacob, of Isaac, of Abraham, of Terah, of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
of Cainan, of Arphaxad, of Shem, of Noah, of Lamech,
of Methuselah, of Enoch, of Jared, of Mahalalel, of Cainan,
the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
Then Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and the Spirit led him into the wilderness.
And for forty days he was tempted by the devil, and he ate nothing during those days. And when those days were over, he was hungry.
And the devil said to him: If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.
Jesus answered and said to him: It is written: A person shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.
And he led him up onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in an image of the times.
And the devil said to him: I will give you authority over all this and their glory, for it has been given to me, and I give it to whomever I wish;
if you worship before me, all of it will be yours.
Jesus answered and said to him, "It is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve."
And he brought him to Jerusalem and set him on the wing of the temple and said to him: If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here to the ground,
for it is written: He has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you,
and they will lift you up with their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.
Jesus answered and said to him: It has been said: You shall not test the Lord your God.
And when the devil had completed all the temptations, he departed from him until a certain time.
And Jesus returned in the power of the Holy Spirit to Galilee, and news of him spread through all the surrounding country.
And he taught in their synagogues and was glorified by all.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and as was his custom he went into their synagogue on the Sabbath day,
and they gave him the book of the prophet Isaiah. And he stood up to read, opened the book, and found the place where it was written:

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal those broken in heart, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to send away the crushed in release,
and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.
And he closed the book, gave it to the attendant, and sat down; and the eyes of the whole assembly were fixed on him.
And he began to say to them: Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.
And all bore witness to him and marveled at the words of grace that came out of his mouth, and they said: Is this not the son of Joseph?
And he said to them: Surely you will say this parable to me: Physician, heal yourself. All that we have heard you did in Capernaum, do here too, in your homeland.
But he said: Amen, I say to you that no prophet is accepted in his own country.
But truly I say to you that there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heavens were shut for three years and six months, when there was a great famine over all the land.
And Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath of Sidon, to a widow woman.
And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was healed except Naaman the Syrian.
And all who were in the synagogue were filled with anger when they heard this.
And they rose up and drove him outside the city and brought him as far as the edge of the mountain on which their city was built, in order to throw him down.
But he passed through their midst and went away.
And he went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and he taught them on the Sabbath.
And they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
And in their synagogue there was a man who had an unclean spirit, and he cried out with a loud voice:
Ah, what is there between us and you, Jesus of Nazareth? You have come to destroy us. We know you, who you are, the Holy One of God.
And Jesus rebuked him and said: Shut your mouth and come out of him! And the demon threw him down in their midst and came out of him and did him no harm.
And amazement came upon them all, and they were discussing with one another and saying, "What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out."
And the report about him was spreading through all the places of the surrounding countryside.
And he rose and left the synagogue and entered the house of Simon. Now Simon's mother-in-law was gripped by a high fever, and they told him about her.
And he stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her immediately, and she rose and served them.
And just as the sun was setting, all who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him. And he laid his hand on each one of them and healed them.
And demons came out of many, crying out and saying, "You are the Christ, the Son of God!" And he rebuked them and did not allow them to speak, for they knew that this was the Christ.
And when day dawned, he came out from there and went away to a desert place, and the crowd was seeking him, and they came to him and tried to hold him back, so that he would not go away from them.
But he said to them, "I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also, for that is why I was sent."
And he was preaching in all the synagogues of Galilee.
It happened that, as the crowd was pressing upon him to hear the word of God, he was standing by the shore of the lake of Gennesaret.
And he saw two boats standing at the shore of the lake; but the fishermen had gotten out of the boat and were washing their nets.
And he got into one of the boats, which was Simon's, and ordered them to put out a little from the land, and he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.
And when he had ceased speaking, he said to Simon, "Put out into the deep and cast your net for a catch."
Simon answered and said to him, "Master, we toiled all night and caught nothing; but at your word let us let down the net."
And they did this and enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were tearing.
And they signalled to those who were in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they were sinking.
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell at the knees of Jesus and said to him, "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord."
For amazement had seized him and all who were with him at the catch of fish which they had taken.
Likewise also James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were partners of Simon. And Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Do not be afraid, Simon! From now on you will be a catcher of men."
And they brought the boat to land and left everything and followed him.

And it happened, when he entered one of the cities, that behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face, begged him, and said to him, "Lord, if you wish, you are able to heal me."
And he stretched out his hand, touched him and said to him: "I am willing; be cleansed!" And immediately the leprosy left him.
And he commanded him to tell no one, but: "Go and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
And the word about him spread abroad all the more. And a great crowd gathered to hear and to be healed of their infirmities.
But he himself would withdraw into the wilderness and pray.

And it happened on one of the days that he was teaching them. And Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and Jerusalem, and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
And behold, men were carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they wanted to bring him in and set him before him.
And they could not find a way to bring him in because of the crowd; they went up on the roof and lifted the man and let him down with the bed into the midst, before Jesus.
And Jesus saw their faith and said to him, "Man, your sins are forgiven you!"
And the scribes and Pharisees began to reason and said, "Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who has authority to forgive sins, except God alone?"
Jesus perceived their thoughts, answered and said to them, "Why do you reason thus in your hearts?"
"What is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Rise and walk'?"
"But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" -- he said to the paralyzed man, "I say to you, rise, take up your bed and go to your house!"
And immediately he got up before them, took up the bed on which he had been lying, and went to his home glorifying God.
And amazement seized everyone, and they glorified God. And fear fell upon them, and they said: "We have seen the greatest glory today."
And after this he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him: Follow me!
And he left everything, got up and followed him.
And Levi prepared a great feast for Jesus in his own house. And there was a great gathering there of tax collectors and of others who were with them, reclining at table.
And the Pharisees and their scribes grumbled to his disciples, saying: "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are in grievous sickness do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, so that they may repent."
But they said to him: Why do the disciples of John fast continually and make supplication, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but your disciples eat and drink?
But Jesus said to them: Surely the sons of the bridegroom are not able, while the bridegroom is with them, to make them fast?
But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken up from them, and then they will fast in those days.
And he also told them a parable: No one puts a patch from a new garment on an old garment, lest he tear the new one, and the patch from the new garment does not match the old one.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins, lest the new wine burst the old wineskins, the wine be spilled, and the wineskins be ruined.
but new wine must be poured into new wineskins, and both are preserved.
And no one who drinks old wine immediately wants new, for he says: The old is sweeter.
And it happened on the second sabbath that he was passing through a sown field. And his disciples were plucking the heads of grain, rubbing them with their hands and eating.
But some of the Pharisees said to them: Why are you doing on the sabbath what is not lawful?
Jesus answered and said to them: Have you not read even this, what David did when he and those with him were hungry,
how he entered the house of God and ate the loaves of offering and also gave them to those with him, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?
And he said to them: The Son of Man is lord of the sabbath also.
And it happened on another sabbath that he entered their synagogue and was teaching. And there was a man there whose right hand was withered.
And the scribes and the Pharisees were watching him, whether he would heal on the sabbath, so that they might find a way to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts, and he said to the man whose hand was withered: Get up and come forward into the middle! And he got up and stood in the middle.
And Jesus said to them: I will ask you something: What is lawful on the sabbath, to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to kill?
And he looked at them all and said to the man: Stretch out your hand! And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, like the other one.
But they were filled with malice and were deliberating with one another what they might do to Jesus.
And it happened in those days that he went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the night in prayer to God.
And when it was day, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he called Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus and Simon, who was called the Zealot,
Judas the son of James and Judas Iscariot, who was the betrayer.
And he came down with them and stood on a level place, and the crowd of his disciples and a very great multitude of other people from Judea and Jerusalem and from the seacoast, from Tyre and Sidon,
who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases; and those afflicted by unclean spirits were being healed.
The whole crowd tried to come near him, because power went out from him, and he healed them all.
And he lifted up his eyes toward his disciples and said to them: Blessed are you poor in spirit, for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled; blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed will you be when people hate you and when they cast you out and revile you and spread abroad your name as that of evildoers, for the sake of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and be glad, for behold, your reward is great in the heavens, for their fathers did the same to the prophets.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation.
Woe to you who are full now, for you will be hungry; woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when all people speak well of you, for in the same way their fathers treated the false prophets well.
But I say to you who hear: love your enemies and do good to those who hate you,
Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
Whoever strikes you on your cheek, offer him the other side as well; and whoever takes your garment from you, do not withhold your tunic from him either.
Give to everyone who asks of you, and from whoever takes from you, do not demand it back.
And just as you wish people to do to you, you also do likewise to them.
And if you love those who love you, what grace is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what grace is that to you? For even sinners do this.
And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive back, what grace is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners, so that they may receive back the equal amount.

But you, love your enemies and do good and lend, and do not make anyone despair, and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he himself is kind even to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged, and do not condemn, so that you may not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven,

Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down and filled and running over, will they give into your bosom; and with the same measure with which you measure out, it will be measured back to you.
He also told them a parable: Surely a blind man is not able to lead a blind man? Will not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not greater than his teacher, but let everyone who is diligent be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye and do not consider the beam of your own eye?

Or how are you able to say to your brother: Brother, allow me, and I will take the speck out of your eye, while you do not see the beam of your own eye? Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
For there is no good tree that brings forth bad fruit, nor again a bad tree that produces good fruit.
For each tree is known by its own fruit; for figs are not gathered from thorns, nor are grapes picked from a bramble.
A good man brings forth good out of the good treasure of his heart, and an evil man brings forth evil out of the evil of his heart; for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks.
Why do you say to me, Lord, Lord, and do not do what I tell you?
Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you whom he is like.
He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid the foundation on rock; and when there was a flood, the river struck that house and could not shake it, for it was founded on rock.
But whoever has heard and does not do is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation; the river struck it, and at once it fell, and the fall of that house was great.
And when Jesus had finished these words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.
And a certain centurion's servant, who was precious to him, was sick and close to death.
And he heard about Jesus and sent elders of the Jews to him to entreat him to come and heal his servant.
Those who came to Jesus pleaded with him earnestly and said to him: "He is worthy for you to do this for him,
for he loves our nation, and he built the synagogue for us."

And Jesus went with them; and when he had come near the house, the centurion sent friends to him and said: Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should come in under the roof of my house.
That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you either. But say it in a word, and this servant of mine will be healed.
For I too am a man placed under authority, and I have soldiers under me; and I say to one: Go! — and he goes; and to another: Come! — and he comes; and to my servant: Do this! — and he does it.
When Jesus heard this, he marveled, and he turned to the crowd that was following him and said: Amen, I say to you, not even in Israel have I found such faith.
And those who had come returned to his house and found his servant alive.
And it happened after this that he was going to a city called Nain, and his disciples and a great crowd were going with him.
And as they drew near to the gates of the city, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only-begotten son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a great crowd from the city was with her.
And the Lord saw the woman and had compassion on her and said to her: Do not weep.
And he came and touched the bier. And those who were carrying it stopped. And he said to him: Young man, I say to you, arise!
And the dead man sat up and began to speak; and he gave him to his mother.
And fear fell upon them all, and they glorified God and said: A great prophet has arisen among us, and God has visited his people.
And this report about him spread through all Judea and all the surrounding region.
And his disciples told John about all these things.
And John called two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus and said: Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?
And when the men came to him, they said to him: John the Baptist has sent us to you and said: Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?
In that hour he healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many who were blind he granted sight.

And Jesus answered and said to them: Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and good news is proclaimed to the poor.
And blessed is he who does not stumble on account of me."
And when John's messengers had gone away, Jesus began to speak to the crowd about John: What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are in splendid clothing and luxury are in royal palaces.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
For this is the one about whom it is written: Behold, I will send my angel before you, who will prepare your ways before you.
I say to you: among those born of women no one is greater than John the prophet, but the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
All the people who heard, and the tax collectors, acknowledged that God was just, having been baptized with John's baptism.
But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law rejected the counsel of God for themselves, for they were not baptized by him.
"To whom shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?
They are like children sitting in the streets, who call [?] to their companions and say: We piped for you, and you did not dance; we mourned for you, and you did not weep.
For John the Baptist came, neither eating nor drinking, and you say: He is possessed by a demon.
The Son of Man came, eating and drinking, and you say: Behold, a man who is a glutton and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.
And wisdom was justified by her children.
One of the Pharisees asked him to eat bread with him; and he went into the Pharisee's house and sat down at table.
And there was a certain woman in that city who was a sinner. She heard that he was in the house of that Pharisee, and she brought ointment in a vessel
And she stood at his feet, weeping, and began to wash his feet and to wipe them with the hair of her head, and she kissed his feet and anointed them with ointment.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he spoke in his heart and said: If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what sort of woman this is who is touching him, for she is a sinner.
Jesus answered and said to him: Simon, I have something to say to you. And he said: Teacher, speak! And he said:
There were two debtors of a certain moneylender. One owed five hundred drachmas, and the other fifty.
Since they had nothing to give, he forgave them both. Now say, which of them will love him more?
Simon answered and said: I suppose it is the one to whom more was forgiven. And he said to him: You have judged rightly.

And he turned to the woman and said to Simon: Do you see this woman? I came into your house, and you did not give me water for my feet, but she has washed my feet with tears and wiped them with her hair;
you did not give me a kiss, but she, from the time she came in, has not ceased kissing my feet;
you did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed me with ointment.
For the sake of which grace I say to you: her many sins are forgiven her, for she has loved me greatly. But the one to whom little is forgiven will also love little.
And he said to her, "Your sins are forgiven you!"
And those reclining at table with him began to say in their hearts: Who is this, who forgives sins?
He said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace!"
And after this he went from city to city and from village to village, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God; and the twelve disciples were with him,
And certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary, who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, who served him from their own produce.
And to the many crowds who were with him, and those who were coming to him from city after city, he spoke in a parable:
A sower went out to sow his seed; and as he sowed, some fell beside the road and was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it.
And other seed fell on rock. It sprang up and withered, because there was no depth of soil.
And other seed fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up and choked it.
And other seed fell on good ground, and it sprang up and produced fruit a hundredfold. This he said aloud: Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
His disciples asked him: What is this parable?
And he said to them: To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to others it comes in parables, so that they may look and not see, and may hear and not understand.
Now this is the parable: the seed is the word of God.
Those along the road are those who hear; then the devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
And those on the rock are those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy, but these have no root; they believe for a time, and in the time of testing they fall away.
And the seed that fell among the thorns stands for those who hear the word, and as they go on they are choked by the cares, riches and pleasures of this world, and they do not bear fruit.
And the seed on the good ground stands for those who hear the word with a good and kind heart, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel, or puts it under a bed; instead they set it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor any secret that will not be known and come out into the open.
So take heed how you hear: whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken from him.
His mother and his brothers came to him, and they could not reach him because of the crowd.
And they told him, saying: Your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to see you.
But he said to them, "My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it."
One day he got into a boat with his disciples, and he said to them, "Let us go across to the other side of the lake." And they set out.
And as they were going in a boat, he fell asleep. And a squall of wind came down upon the sea, and the boat was filling, and they were in distress.
They came to him and woke him, saying to him: Teacher, we are perishing. And he arose and rebuked the wind and the waves of the waters; and it ceased, and there was a great calm.
He said to them, "Where is your faith?" They were afraid and amazed, and said to one another, "Who then is this, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?"
And they went out to the country of the Gergesenes, which is on the far side from Galilee.
As they stepped out onto land, a man from the city met him, who had demons in him. For a long time he had worn no clothes, and he did not live in a house but among the tombs.
And when he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell at Jesus's feet and said in a loud voice: What is there between me and you, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I beg you, do not torment me.

For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him; they would bind him with chains and fetters and guard him, but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon into the wilderness.
Jesus asked him: What is your name? And he said: Legion, for many demons had entered into him.
And they begged him not to command them to fall down into the abysses.
And there was there a herd of many pigs, feeding on the mountain; and they begged him to command them to enter into those pigs. And he commanded them.
And the demons came out of the man and went into the swine. And the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and were drowned.
When the herdsmen saw this thing, they fled and told it in the city and in the villages.
And they came out to see what had happened, and they came to Jesus and saw the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
For those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been healed.

And all the multitude of the surrounding country of the Gergesenes begged him to depart from their territory, for they were seized with great fear. And he got into a boat and returned to the same place.
But the man from whom the demons had been cast out begged him that he might be with him. But he sent him away and said to him:
"Return to your home and tell how much God has done for you." And he went away and preached in all those cities what Jesus had done for him.
And when Jesus returned there, the crowd welcomed him, for they were waiting for him.
And behold, a man came, and his name was Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue; he fell at the feet of Jesus and begged him to come into his house.
for he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As he went, the crowds pressed around him.
And there was a certain woman with a flow of blood for twelve years, who could not be healed by anyone.
She came up from behind and touched the fringe of his garment. And immediately the flow of her blood stopped.
And Jesus said: "Who touched me?" And as all were denying it, Peter said to him: "Teacher, the crowds surround you and press in on you, and you say: Who touched me?"
But Jesus said: "Someone touched me, for I perceived power gone out from me."

And when the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling and fell down before him, and she told before all the people for what cause she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
And Jesus said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace!"
And while he was still speaking, someone came from the ruler of the synagogue and said to him: "Your daughter has died; do not trouble the teacher."
But when Jesus heard this, he said to him: "Do not be afraid, only believe, and she will be saved."
And when he came to the house, he let no one go in with him except Peter and James and John, and the father and mother of the child.
All were weeping for her and beating themselves in mourning. But Jesus said to them: "Do not weep, for the child is not dead, but is sleeping."
And they laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
And he put them all out, took the child by the hand, and called out: "Child, arise!"
And her spirit returned, and she immediately arose. And he commanded that they give her food.
And her parents were amazed. But he instructed them to tell no one what had happened.
And he called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons and for the healing of diseases.
And he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
And he said to them: "Have nothing for the road: neither bags, nor bread, nor silver, nor have two garments."
"And whatever house you enter, stay there and go out from there."
"And as many as do not receive you, when you go out from that city, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony to them."
So they went out and travelled through the villages, preaching the good news and healing the sick everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard of the things that were being done by him, and he pondered, because some were saying: "John the Baptist has risen from the dead."
But some were saying, "Elijah has appeared," and others were saying, "One of the prophets of old has risen."
But Herod said, "I beheaded John; but who this is, about whom I hear such things, I do not know." And he wanted to see him.
And the apostles returned and told Jesus how much they had done. And he took them and withdrew privately to a place belonging to a city called Bethsaida.
But the crowd perceived it and followed him. And he received them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed as many as needed healing.

And as the day began to decline, the disciples came to him and said to him, "Send this crowd away, so that they may go to the surrounding villages and farms and stay there and find food for themselves, for here we are in a desert place."
But Jesus said to them, "You give them something to eat." And they said, "We have no more than five loaves of bread and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all this people."
For the men were about five thousand. And Jesus said to his disciples, "Have those men sit down in dining groups, fifty to a group."
And they did so and seated them all.
And he himself took the five loaves and the two fish, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and blessed them, and broke them, and kept giving them to the disciples to set before the people.
And they all ate and were filled, and they took up what was left over to them of the fragments, twelve baskets.
And it happened, as he was praying by himself, that the disciples were with him. And he questioned them and said, "Who do these people think I am? What do they say about me?"
And they answered and said to him, "John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and some say that one of the prophets of old has risen."
And Jesus said to them, "But who do you think I am?" Peter answered and said to him, "The Anointed One of God."
But he rebuked them and commanded them to tell this to no one.
And he said to them, "The Son of Man must suffer much and be treated with contempt by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and on the third day rise."
And he said to all, "Whoever wishes to follow me, let him deny himself and take up his cross day by day and follow me."
For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
What profit is it to a person if he gains the whole world and destroys himself or suffers loss?
Whoever is ashamed of me and of these my words, the Son of Man too will put him to shame when he comes in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels.
I tell you truly: there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.
And it happened, about eight days after these words, that he took Peter and James and John and went up on a mountain to pray.
And as he was praying, the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing white as lightning.
And behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
who appeared in glory and were speaking of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
But Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep; and when they woke up, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

And as they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents: one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah" — for he did not know what he was saying.
And as he was saying this, behold, a cloud overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
And a voice came out of the cloud: "This is my chosen Son; listen to him!"
And when this voice had come, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent and in those days told no one anything of what they had seen.
And it happened on the next day, as they came down from the mountain, that a great crowd came to meet him.
And behold, a certain man cried out among the crowd and said, "Master, I beg you, look upon my son, for he is the only one I have."
And an evil spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it convulses him, and he foams, and it departs from him with difficulty and crushes him.
"And I begged your disciples to drive it out, and they could not."
But Jesus said: O perverse generation! How long am I to be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here to me!
And while he was coming, the demon struck him down and threw him into convulsions. And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
And all were astonished at the majesty of God, and all were amazed at everything that Jesus was doing. And Jesus said to his disciples:
Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men.
But they did not understand that saying, and it was hidden from them so that they could not grasp it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
A thought also entered their minds: who might be the greatest among them?
But Jesus knew the thoughts of their hearts, and he brought a child and stood him before himself.
And he said: Whoever receives this child in my name has received me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me, for the one who is least among all of you is the one who is great.
And John answered and said to him: Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow along with us.
Jesus said to him: Do not stop him, for whoever is not our enemy is on our side.
And it came to pass, when the days of his ascension were being fulfilled, that he himself set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
And he sent messengers ahead of him. And they went and entered a village of the Samaritans, to make preparations for him.
And they did not receive them, because his face was set toward going to Jerusalem.
And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said: Lord, do you wish us to speak, so that fire may come down from heaven and wipe them out, as Elijah did?
Jesus turned, rebuked them, and said to them: Do you not know of what spirit you are?
For the Son of Man did not come to destroy the souls of men, but to give them life. And they went on to another village.
And as they were going along the road, someone said to him: I will follow you wherever you go.
Jesus said to him: Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have dwellings, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.
And to another he said: Follow me! And he said: Lord, permit me first to bury my father.
Jesus said to him: Let the dead bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim far and wide the kingdom of God.
Another also said to him: I will follow you, Lord, but first permit me to take leave of my household.
Jesus said to him: No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.
And after this the Lord appointed another seventy-two, and sent them two by two ahead of him to every city and village where he himself was about to go.
And he said to them: The harvest is great, but the laborers are few. Therefore pray to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out laborers into his harvest.
Go! Behold, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a purse, nor bags, nor footwear, and greet no one on the road.
Whatever house you enter, first say: 'Peace to this house!'
And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; if not, it will return to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking with them, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Do not go from house to house.
And whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you.
and heal the sick in it, and say to them: 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
And whatever city you enter, if they do not receive you, as you come out from there into its streets, say to them:
Behold, the dust from your city that has clung to our feet we shake off against you; yet know this, that the kingdom of God has drawn near.
I say to you: it will be more bearable for the Sodomites on that day than for that city.
Woe to you, Chorazin, and woe to you, Bethsaida, for if the mighty works that were done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth on ashes.
But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, do not exalt yourself to heaven, for you will go down as far as hell.
Whoever hears you has heard me; and whoever despises you despises me; and whoever despises me despises the one who sent me.
And the seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name."
Jesus said to them: I was watching the devil, fallen down from heaven like lightning.
Behold, I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice in this, that evil spirits are subject to you; rather rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens.

At that hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said: I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned and have revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was pleasing before you.

All things have been given to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son, and the one to whom the Son wishes to reveal him, to him he will reveal him.
And he turned to his disciples privately and said to them: Blessed are the eyes that see what you see, and the ears that hear what you hear.
But I tell you that many prophets and kings wished to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.
And behold, a certain lawyer stood up, testing him and saying to him: Teacher, what shall I do so that I may inherit eternal life?
And he himself said to him: How is it written in the Law? How do you read it?
And he said, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself."
Jesus said to him: "You have answered rightly. Do this, and you will live."
But he wanted to justify himself, and he said to Jesus: "And who is my neighbour?"
Jesus answered and said to him: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and robbers fell upon him and stripped him and wounded him, and they went away and left him half-dead.
A certain priest was going down by that same road, and he came upon him and saw him and passed by.
And likewise a Levite came to the same place, saw him, and passed by.
Then a certain Samaritan was traveling, came to the same place, saw him, and had compassion on him.
And he came to him and bound up his wound and poured on oil and wine, and he lifted him onto his own pack animal and brought him to an inn and took care of him.

And on the next day, as he was departing, he gave two drachmas to the keeper of that inn and said to him: Take care of him, and if you spend anything more besides, when I come back, then I will give it to you.
Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?
And he said: The one who showed mercy to him. Jesus said to him: Go, and you too do likewise.
And as they went away, he himself entered a certain village, and there was a certain woman whose name was Martha, and she brought him into her house.
And she had a sister called Mary, who sat at Jesus' feet and listened to his words.
But Martha was busily occupied with much serving, and she came up and said to Jesus: Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me alone to serve? Tell her to help me.
Jesus answered and said to her: Martha, Martha! You are anxious and troubled about many things;
and here little is needed. But Mary has chosen the good portion, which will never be taken from her.
And he himself was in a certain place and was praying. And when he had ceased from prayer, one of his disciples said to him: Lord, teach us prayer, just as John taught his disciples.
And he himself said to them: When you pray, say: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done.
Give us our essential bread day by day.
And forgive us our sins, for we too forgive all our debtors, and do not lead us into temptation.
And he said to them: "Which of you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight and says to him: 'Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
For a friend has come to me from the road, and I have nothing to set before him.
And he will answer from within and say to him: Do not bring trouble on me, for the door is shut and my children are with me in bed; I cannot get up and give to you.
I tell you: even though he cannot get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his annoying persistence he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
And I tell you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Which father among you, then, if his son asks him for bread, would give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, would give him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, would give him a scorpion?
If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.
And he drove out of a certain man a demon that was mute. And it happened that when the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke. And all the crowd were amazed.
But some of them said: "He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of demons."
And others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
But he himself knew their thoughts and said to them: Every kingdom that is divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.
And if the devil has been divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand firm? For you say about me that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
If I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves will be your judges.
If I cast out demons by the finger of God, has not the kingdom of God indeed come upon you?
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his goods are in peace.
And when one stronger than he comes upon him and overcomes him, he takes away his armor, in which he trusted, and divides his spoils.
Whoever is not with me is my enemy; and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it wanders through waterless places and seeks a place of rest and does not find one, and it says: I will return to my house, from which I came out.
And when it comes, it finds it swept and adorned.
It goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and settle in him, and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first.
And it happened, while he was still saying this, that a certain woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him: Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts at which you nursed!
But he said to her, "Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it."
And as the crowd was gathering to him, he began to say to them: This generation is an evil generation; it asks for a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
Just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will the Son of Man be to this generation.

The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the people of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah. And behold, one greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place, but on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light.
The lamp of the body is your eye; when your eye is sound, your whole body will be light. If your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark.
See to it, then, that the light in you is not darkness.
If your whole body is light and has no part that is dark, it will be entirely light, as when a lamp gives you light with its flash.
And as he was saying this, a certain Pharisee asked him to eat a meal with him; and he went in and sat down at the table.
But when the Pharisee saw this, he was astonished that he had not first washed before eating the meal.
The Lord said to him: Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
Fools, did not he who made the outside also make the inside?
But give as alms what is proper, and behold, everything of yours is clean.
But woe to you, Pharisees! For you take a tithe of mint and rue and every herb, and you pass over justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.
Woe to you, Pharisees, for you love sitting in the highest place in the synagogues and being greeted in the streets.
Woe to you, for you are like unseen graves, and people walk over them and do not know it.
A certain lawyer answered and said to him: Teacher, in saying this you insult us too.
But he said to them: Woe to you also, lawyers, for you load people with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch that burden with even one of your fingers.
Woe to you, for you build the tomb of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.
So you bear witness and give approval to the deeds of your fathers; for they killed them, and you build their tombs.
For this reason the Wisdom of God also said: I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,
so that the blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, who perished between the altar and the temple — yes, I tell you — it will be required of this generation.
Woe to you, teachers of the law, for you have hidden the keys of knowledge; you yourselves do not enter, and you hinder those who are entering.
And as he was saying this to them before all the people, those scribes and Pharisees began to plot evil, and that word was grievous to them, and they reviled him because of his many words.
And they watched him, to catch some word from his mouth, so that they might accuse him.

Meanwhile a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. He began first to say to his disciples: Beware for yourselves of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
But there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
Therefore what you say in the darkness will be heard in the light; and what you speak into the ear in the inner storerooms will be proclaimed on the rooftops.
And I tell you, my friends: do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more that they can do to you.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear him who, after killing, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? And not one of them is hidden before God.
But even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid, for you are better than many sparrows.
And I tell you: everyone who confesses me before men, the Son of Man too will confess him before the angels of God.
And whoever denies me before people, he too will be denied before the angels of God.
And everyone who speaks a word concerning the Son of Man will be forgiven, but the one who blasphemes the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
And when they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry how or what word you should answer, or what you should say.
For the Holy Spirit will teach you in that hour what you should say.
Someone from the crowd said to him: Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.
But he said to him: Man, who appointed me judge and divider over you?
And he said to them: Beware and guard yourselves from all greed, for a person's life does not come from the abundance of his produce.
And he also told them a parable and said to them: The farmland of a certain man was fruitful.
And he reasoned in his heart and said: What shall I do, for I have nowhere to gather my fruits?
'I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather there all my fruit and my goods.'
And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many good things stored up for many years: rest, eat, drink, and rejoice.
God said to him: Fool, this night they will take your soul from you; and what you have prepared, whose will it be?
So also is the one who stores up treasure for himself and does not grow rich toward God.
And he said to his disciples: Therefore I say to you: do not be anxious about your soul, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on,
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Consider the ravens, for they neither sow nor reap, they have no storehouse or place to gather into, and God feeds them. How much better are you than the birds?
Which of you, then, by being anxious, could add one cubit to his stature?
If you are not able to do even the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
Consider the lily, how it grows: it neither toils nor spins. But I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If God so adorned the grass in the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven and burned, how much more you, you of little faith?
And do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be restless [?],
for the peoples of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows that you need all of these.
But seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give alms, and make for yourselves wealth that does not grow old, and an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Let your loins be girded and your lamps lit.
And be like those people who wait for their master, for when he may come from the wedding, so that, when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once.
Blessed are those servants whose master comes and finds them awake; amen I say to you that he will gird himself and seat them, and will come forward and serve them.
And even if he comes in the second watch or the third and finds them so, blessed are they.
But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief would come, he would have kept watch and would not have let the wall of his house be dug through.
You also must be ready, for the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
Peter said to him: Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone?
And Jesus said to him: Who then is the faithful steward, whom the master will set over his servants to give them their measure of wheat at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whose lord comes and finds him doing so.
Amen, I tell you, he will set him over all his possessions.
But if that servant says in his heart: My master is delaying his coming, and begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, to eat and drink and get drunk,
the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the unbelievers.
But the servant who knows his master's will and does not prepare himself according to his will shall be punished severely.

But the one who does not know and does something deserving punishment shall be beaten a little, for from everyone to whom much was given, much will also be required, and from the one to whom a great deal was given, they will demand all the more.
I came to spread fire upon the earth, and what do I wish, but that it were already kindled!
But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
Do you suppose that I have come to spread peace upon the earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.
For from now on there will be five in one house, divided: three against two and two against three.
Father will be divided from son and son from father, mother from daughter and daughter from mother, mother-in-law from her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law from mother-in-law.
Jesus also said to the crowd: When you see a cloud rising from the west, you immediately say, "It is bringing rain," and so it happens.
And when the wind blows from the south, you say, "There will be heat," and so it happens.
Hypocrites! You know how to judge the face of the earth and of the sky, so why do you not judge this present time?
Or why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For when you go with your adversary before the ruler, make an effort on the way to be set free from him. Otherwise he may drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer put you in prison.
I tell you: you will not come out from there until you have paid even the last small coin.
At that very time some people came and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Jesus answered and said to them: Do you suppose that these Galileans were greater sinners than all the Galileans, because they suffered such a thing?
I tell you, no. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower in Siloam fell on them: do you think that they were more guilty than all the other people who live in Jerusalem?
I tell you: no; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
And Jesus told this parable: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and found none.

And he said to the vinedresser: Look, it is three years now that I have been coming and looking for fruit on this fig tree, and I have found none. Cut it down; why should it even occupy the ground uselessly?
But he answered and said to him: Lord, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put down manure,
and perhaps it will produce fruit; if not, then I will cut it down.
And Jesus was teaching them in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; and she was bent over and could not look upward at all.
Jesus saw her, and he called her and said to her: Woman, you are released from your infirmity.
And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood upright and walked, and she glorified God.

But the leader of the synagogue, angry that Jesus had healed her on the sabbath, answered and said to the people, “There are six days on which it is right to work. Come on those days and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.”
Jesus answered him and said: Hypocrite, does not each one of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from its manger and lead it away and give it water?
And this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen years now, should she not have been set free from her bonds on the sabbath day?”
And as he said this, all his adversaries were put to shame; and all the people rejoiced at all the glorious things that were being done by him.
And the Lord said: To what shall I liken the kingdom of God, and whom does it resemble?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky settled in its branches.
And again he said, “What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?
It is like leaven, which a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until it leavened the whole.
And he went about through towns and villages, teaching, as he journeyed toward Jerusalem.
And someone said to him: "Lord, are those who are saved few?" And he said to them:
"Strive to enter through the narrow gate. For I tell you: many will seek to enter and will not be able.

Once the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you stand outside and begin to knock at the door and say, "Lord, Lord, open to us!", he will answer and say to you: I do not know you, who you are.
Then you will begin to say: 'We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught us in our streets.'
And he will say to you: I do not know who you are; depart from me, all you workers of lawlessness!
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and you cast outside.
And they will come from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south, and will [?] in the kingdom of God.
And behold, there are last who were first, and there are first who were last.
On that day some Pharisees came up to Jesus and said to him: Go out and depart from here, for Herod seeks to kill you.
But he himself said to them: Go and tell that fox: Behold, I cast out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will be finished.
For I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the day after, because it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How many times I have wanted to gather your children, as a bird gathers its chicks under its wings, and you were not willing!
Behold, your houses are left to you desolate. I say to you: you will not see me again from now on until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'
And it happened, when Jesus came to the house of a certain ruler of the Pharisees on the Sabbath day to eat bread, that they were watching him.
And behold, there was before him a certain man afflicted with dropsy.
Jesus answered and said to the teachers of the Law and the Pharisees: "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"
But they were silent. And he brought the man forward, healed him, and sent him away.
And he said to them: Which of you, if his son or his ox falls into a pit, will not immediately pull him out on the Sabbath day?
And they could give him no answer to this.
And he told a parable to those who had been invited, as he observed how they were choosing the upper seats, and he said to them:
When someone invites you to a wedding, do not sit down in the first place at table, lest someone more honorable than you has been invited by him;
and the one who invited both you and him comes and says to you, 'Give your place to this man!' Then you will begin, in shame, to take the last place.

but when someone invites you, go and sit in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, go up higher!' Then you will have glory before all your fellow guests.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

He also said to the one who had invited him: When you make a dinner or a supper, do not invite your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor your rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and it become your repayment.
But when you make a dinner, invite the poor, the ignorant, the lame, the blind,
and you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you, and you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.
