One of those sitting at table with him heard this and said to him: "Blessed is he who will eat bread in the kingdom of God."
But he said to him: "A certain man gave a great supper and invited many people.
And at the hour of the meal he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited to come, for behold, everything is ready.
And each and every one of them began to make excuses. The first said to him: I have bought a field, and I am under necessity to go and see it. I beg you, release me; let me be excused by you.
And another said: I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. I beg you, let me be excused.
And then another said, 'I have married a wife, and for that reason I cannot come.'

And the servant came and told this to his lord. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, the strangers, the blind and the lame.
And the servant said: Lord, your command has been carried out, and there is still room.
And the lord said to the servant: Go out onto the roads and paths and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.
But I say to you: none of those men will taste of this supper of mine.
And a great crowd was gathering to him. And he turned and said to them:
Whoever comes to me and does not hate his father and his mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and furthermore even his own self, cannot be my disciple.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate how much it will cost, whether he has enough to suffice him for completing it?
Otherwise he may lay the foundation and be unable to complete it, and all who see him will begin to mock him
and say: This man began to build and was unable to complete it.
Or what king, going to battle against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
If not, while the other is still far away, he sends an envoy to him and greets him in peace.
So also, every one of you who does not part from all his possessions cannot be my disciple.
Salt is good. But if the salt loses its savour, with what will it be salted?
It is of no use either for the ground or for the dunghill, but they throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to listen to him.
And the Pharisees and the scribes grumbled and said, "This man receives sinners and eats and drinks with them."
And he told them this parable, saying:
What man among you who has a hundred sheep and loses one of them will not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
And when he finds it, he lays it on his shoulders with joy.
And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbors and says to them: Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep.
I tell you: in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.
Or what woman who has ten drachmas, that is, staters, and loses one stater, will not light a lamp and set the house in order and search diligently until she finds it?
And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors and says to them: Rejoice with me, for I have found the stater that I had lost.
I tell you, in the same way there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
Then he spoke again and said: A certain man had two sons.
And the younger one said to his father: Give me the share of the inheritance that falls to me. And he divided his livelihood between them.
And not many days later the younger son gathered everything together and went away to a distant country, and there he squandered his wealth, for he lived impurely.
And when he had lost everything he had, there was a severe famine in that country. And he began to be in need.
And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
And his heart urged him to fill his belly with the carob pods that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him anything.
He reflected within himself and said: How many of my father's hired men have bread to spare, and here I am perishing of hunger.
I will get up and go to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
And I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your laborers.
And he got up and went to his father. And while he was still far off, his father saw him and had pity on him, and he ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
The son said to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son.
His father said to his servants: Bring out the best robe and clothe him in it, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
And bring the fat calf and slaughter it, and let us eat and rejoice.
For this son of mine was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found. And they began to make merry.
And his elder son was out in the field. And as he was coming and drew near the house, he heard the sound of rejoicing and merrymaking.
And he called one of the servants and asked him, "What is this?"
And he said to him: Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf, because he has got him back alive.
But he became angry and would not go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

And he answered and said to his father: Look, all these years I have served you and have never disobeyed your command, and you have never given me a single kid so that I might rejoice with my friends.
And when this son of yours came, who devoured your livelihood with harlots, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.
But he said to him: Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
But now it is right to make merry and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found."
And he also said to the disciples: There was a certain rich man who had a steward. And this man was denounced to him for squandering his wealth.
And he called him and said to him: What is this that I hear about you? Give me the account of your stewardship, for from now on you can no longer be steward.
Then the steward said in his heart: What shall I do, since my lord is taking my stewardship away from me? I do not have the strength to work, and I am ashamed to beg.
Now I know what I shall do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they will receive me into their households.
And he called each one of his lord's debtors and said to the first: How much do you owe my lord?
And he said: A hundred presses of oil. And he said to him: Take your bond, sit down quickly and write fifty.
Then he said to another: And you, how much do you owe? And he said to him: A hundred measures of thirty of wheat. He said to him also: Take your bond and write eighty.
And the lord praised that steward of falsehood, because he had acted prudently. For the sons of this world are more prudent than the sons of light in their generation.
And I say to you: Make friends for yourselves from this mammon of falsehood, so that when you fail and pass from this world, they may receive you into those eternal dwellings.
The one who is faithful in little is faithful in much as well; and the one who is false in little is false in much as well.
If you do not prove faithful with this mammon of falsehood, who will entrust the true to you?
And if you do not prove faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
No servant can serve two lords: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other. One cannot serve God and mammon.
The Pharisees heard all this, for they were lovers of silver, and they scorned him.
And he said to them: You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts, for what is exalted among men is abominable before God.
The law and the prophets were until John: from then on the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone is pressing toward it.
It is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the law to fall.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and he who marries a woman divorced from her husband also commits adultery.
There was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen and rejoiced splendidly day after day.
There was a certain poor man named Lazarus, who lay at his gates and was covered with sores [?].
And his heart longed to be filled with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table, but even the dogs came and licked his wounds.
It came to pass that the poor man died, and he was carried by angels to the bosom of Abraham; the rich man also died and was buried.
And in hell he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham from afar and Lazarus in his bosom.
And he cried out and said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am tormented in this flame of fire.
But Abraham said to him: Child, remember that you received your good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise evil things. And now behold, he is comforted here, but you are tormented.
And besides all this, a great chasm is fixed between us and you, so that those who wish to cross over from here to you cannot, nor can they cross from there to us.
Then he said: I beg you, father, send him to my father's house,
for I have five brothers, so that he may warn them, and they too may not come to this place of torment.
Abraham said to him: They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.
But he said to him: No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.
Abraham said to him: If they did not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they believe even if someone rises from the dead.
Jesus said to his disciples: It is impossible for stumbling blocks not to come, but woe to the one through whom they come.
It would be easier for him if a millstone were laid on his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
But take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
And even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times turns back and says to you, 'I have repented,' forgive him.
The apostles said to the Lord: Increase our faith!
Jesus said to them: If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would say to this wild fig tree, 'Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Which of you, having a servant who is plowing or shepherding, when he has come in from the field, would say to him at once: Come here and sit down?
Rather, he will say to him: Prepare something for me so that I may dine, and gird yourself and serve me until I have eaten and drunk, and after this you too eat and drink.
Will he thank that servant because he did what he commanded? I do not think so.
So you also, when you do what has been commanded you, say: We are worthless servants; we have done what it was laid upon us to do.
And it happened as he was going to Jerusalem that he passed through between Samaria and Galilee.
And as he entered a certain village, ten leprous men met him, who stood at a distance,
And they raised their voices and said, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
and when he saw them, he said to them: Go, show yourselves to the priests. And it happened that as soon as they went away from him, they were cleansed of the leprosy.
But one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back and glorified God with a loud voice.
And he fell down before his feet and thanked him. And this man was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered and said to him, "Were not all ten healed? And where are the nine?"
Were not so many found who would turn back and give glory to God, except only this foreigner?
And he said to him, "Rise and go! Your faith has saved you."
The Pharisees asked him: When will the kingdom of God come? Jesus answered them and said: The kingdom of God will not come by observation;
nor will they say: Behold, here, or there. For behold, the kingdom of God is among you.
And he said to the disciples, "The days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
And they will say to you: Behold, it is here, and: Behold, it is there. Do not go out.
For as the lightning flashes from under the heaven and shines as far as under it, so will the Son of Man be in his days.
But first he must suffer much and be despised by this generation.
And as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man:
they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark. And the flood came and destroyed them all.
And likewise, as it was in the days of Lot: they were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
And on the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone and destroyed them all.
So will that day be when the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever is on the roof, with his goods in the house, let him not come down to take them; and whoever is out in the field, let him not turn back again.
Remember the wife of Lot.
Whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses it will keep it alive.
I tell you: on that night two will be in one bed: the one will be snatched away, and the other will be left;
Two will be grinding together: one will be taken, and the other will be left."
And they answered and said to him: Where, Lord? But he said to them: Wherever the body is, there too the eagles will gather.
He also told them a parable, to show that they ought always to pray and not grow weary in prayer.
And he said: There was a certain judge in a city who did not fear God and was not ashamed before people.
And there was a widow in that same city. And she kept coming to him and saying to him: Give me justice against my adversary.
And he would not listen to her for some time. After this he said in his heart: Although I do not fear God and am not ashamed before men,
yet because this widow is constantly causing me trouble, I will give her justice, so that she may not keep coming continually and wearying me.
And the Lord said to them: Hear now what the judge of falsehood says.
And will God not avenge his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night, and is he long-suffering toward them?
I tell you: he will avenge them quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?
He spoke this parable to certain people who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and who despised others,
saying: Two men went up to the temple to pray: one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed this by himself: God, I thank you that I am not like other men, a robber, a liar, an adulterer, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week, and I offer a tithe of everything I acquire.
But the tax collector stood far off and did not dare even to lift his eyes to heaven, but he beat his breast and said: Lord, have mercy on this sinner.
I tell you: this man went down to his house justified rather than that Pharisee, for whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
They were also bringing children to him, so that they might come near him. And when the disciples saw it, they tried to stop them.
But Jesus called them and said: Let these children come to me and do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Amen, I say to you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will not be able to enter it.
And a certain ruler asked him and said: Good teacher, what deed shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honour your father and your mother.
And he said: I have kept all these from my youth.
When Jesus heard this, he said to him: One thing you still lack: sell all that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens, and come, follow me.
And when he heard this, he became sorrowful, for he was very rich.
When Jesus saw him, he said: How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God.
It is easier for a ship's cable to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
But those who heard it said to him: Then who can be saved?
Jesus answered and said: What is impossible for people is possible for God.
Peter said to him: Look, we have left everything of our own and followed you.
But Jesus said to them: Amen, I say to you, there is no one who has left house, or father, or mother, or brothers, or wife, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
who will not receive many portions in this present time, and in the age to come, eternal life.
And he took the twelve aside and said to them: Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
For he will be handed over to the Gentiles, and they will mock him, and insult him, and spit on him,
and they will torment him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise again."
But they did not understand this; that saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was said.
And it happened that as they drew near to Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting by the road begging.
When he heard that a crowd was coming by, he asked: What is this?
And they told him: Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.
But he cried out and said: Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me!
Those who were walking in front rebuked him, telling him to be quiet. But he cried out all the more and said, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
And Jesus stopped and ordered that he be called. And when he drew near, he said to him:
What do you wish me to do for you? And he said: Lord, that I may recover the sight of my eyes.
And Jesus said to him, "Receive your sight! Your faith has saved you."
And at once he regained his sight, and he followed him, glorifying God. And all the people saw it and praised God.
And he entered and was passing through Jericho.
And look, there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was very rich.
And he wanted to see Jesus, who he was, and he could not see because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
And he ran on ahead and climbed up a sycamore-fig tree in order to see him, for he was going to pass by that way.
And he came to that place, and Jesus looked up and said to him: Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay in your house.
And he hurried and came down and brought him in with joy.
And when they all saw it, they grumbled and said: He has gone in to lodge with a sinful man.
Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, I will give half of my goods to the poor; and if I have falsely accused anyone, I will pay him back fourfold."
Jesus said to him: Today salvation has come to this house, for this man too is a descendant of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save what was lost.
And as the people were hearing this, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they supposed that the kingdom of God would appear immediately.
And he said to them: A certain nobleman was going to a distant country to receive kingship for himself and to return.
He called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas, and said to them: 'Trade with this until I come.'
But his citizens hated him, and they sent an envoy after him and said to him: We do not want that man's reign over us.
And it happened on his return, having received his kingship, that he ordered those servants to whom he had given the silver to be called, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.
And the first came and said: Lord, your silver has gained ten more pounds.
He said to him: Well done, good servant; because you were faithful in a small matter, be ruler over ten cities.
And the second came and said: Lord, your silver has made five more pounds.
He said to him also: You too be over five cities.
And the third came and said: Lord, here is your silver, which I kept stored away in a cloth,
For I was afraid, because you are a harsh man: you take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.
He said to him: By your own mouth I will judge you, faithless servant. You knew that I am a harsh man: I take up what I did not lay down, and I reap where I did not sow.
Then why did you not put my silver on the trading table, so that I would have come and collected it with interest?
And he said to those standing by: Take the silver from him and give it to the one who has ten pounds of silver.
And they said to him: 'Lord, he has ten pounds.'
"But I tell you: to whoever has, more will be given; but from whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
But as for those enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here to me and slaughter them before me.
And when he had said this, he went on ahead of them, going up to Jerusalem.
And it happened that, as he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount that is called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples
And he said to them: Go into that village ahead of you; when you enter it you will find a colt tied, on which no man has ever sat. Untie it and bring it to me.
And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?', say this: 'The Lord has need of it.'
And when those whom he had sent went, they found it just as he had told them.
And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: Why are you untying that colt?
And they said, "The Lord needs it."
And they brought it to Jesus, and they threw their garments on the colt, and Jesus sat on it.
And as he went in, they spread their garments on the road.
And as he reached the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began joyfully to praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen.
and they said, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"
And some Pharisees from the crowd said to him: Teacher, rebuke your disciples!
But Jesus said to them: I tell you, even if these were to keep silent, the stones would cry out.
And as he drew near, he saw the city and wept over it,
and he said, "If only you had known on this day what makes for your peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when the army of your enemies will come up against you, surround you, and hem you in on every side.
And they will tear you down, and your children within you will fall, and no stone will be left upon a stone within you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.
And when he entered the temple, he began to drive out those who were selling doves.
And he said to them: "It is written: 'My house shall be a house of prayer,' but you have made it a den of robbers."
And he was there, teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the leaders of the people sought to destroy him.
and they could not find anything they might do to him, for all the people were devoted to listening to him.
And it happened in those days, as he was teaching the people and proclaiming the good news in the temple, that the chief priests and the scribes, together with the elders, came up to him,
and they spoke to him and said: "Tell us, by what authority do you do these things, or who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered and said to them: I will ask you something, and you tell me:
Was the baptism of John from heaven, or from men?
But they conferred with one another, saying: If we say, 'It was from heaven,' he will say to us, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
And if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us, for John is held to be a prophet.
They answered and said: We do not know where it was from.
And Jesus said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do this."
And he began to speak to them in a parable: A certain man planted a vineyard, and gave it to tenants, and went away for a long time.
And at the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants, so that they would give him some of its fruit. But the tenants beat him and tormented him and sent him away empty-handed.
And he went on to send another servant. But they beat him too and sent him away empty-handed.
Then he sent a third again. But they seized him and inflicted wounds on him and drove him out.
And the lord of the vineyard said: What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; who knows, perhaps they will respect him.
But when the tenants saw him, they conferred with one another and said: This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance may be ours.
And they took him outside the vineyard and killed him. Now what will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others." But when they heard this, they said, "May it never be!"
But he looked at them and said: What then is this that is written: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be shattered; and on whomever it falls, it will scatter him like chaff.
And the chief priests and the scribes wanted to lay their hands on him at that time, and they were afraid of the people, for they understood that he had told this parable about them.
And they watched him and sent spies, treacherous men who declared themselves righteous, so that they might find some word against him and hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
And they questioned him and said to him: Teacher, we know that you speak what is right and teach it, and you show partiality to no one, but you teach the way of God in truth.
Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?"
And he saw through their cunning and said to them, "Why do you test me?
Show me a denarius! Whose image and inscription does it bear? And they said to him: Caesar's.
And Jesus said to them, "Then give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
And they found no word to answer him before the people. And they marveled at his reply and fell silent.
Then some of the Sadducees, who dispute, saying that there is no resurrection, came to him at that time and questioned him and said to him:
Teacher, Moses wrote this for us: If someone's brother dies, having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers among us. The first took a wife and died childless.
And the second and the third.
And they died childless. And likewise all seven of them, and no child was left.
And after them the woman also died.
Now then, in the resurrection of the dead, whose wife among them will she be, for all seven had her as wife?
Jesus answered and said to them, "The children of this world marry and are given in marriage;
But those who have become worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
Nor can they die anymore, for they are equal to the angels and are sons of God and sons of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, Moses also made known at the bush, when he speaks of the Lord as the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
For God is not of the dead but of the living, for all are alive before him.
Some of the scribes answered and said to him: "Teacher, you have spoken well."
And from then on they no longer dared to question him. And the Lord said to them:
How then do some of you say that the Christ is the son of David?
For David himself says in the Book of Psalms: 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool under your feet.'
David himself calls him Lord, so how is he his son?
And as all the people were listening, he said to his disciples:
Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in robes and who love greetings in the streets and the first seats in the assembly and the upper seats at meals,
who devour the houses of widows and, as a pretext, pray at great length. These will receive the greater condemnation."
And he looked up and saw the rich who were putting their offerings into the treasury.
And he saw a poor widow who put in two mites.
And he said: Truly I tell you that this poor widow has offered more than all of them.
For all these offered into this collection out of their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, offered all the living she had."
And some were saying about the temple that it was built with fine and precious stone; and Jesus said:
Do you see this? But days will come in which no stone will be left upon a stone that will not be torn down.
The disciples asked him: Teacher, when will this be, and what is the sign when this is about to happen?
But he said to them: See that you are not led astray, for many will come in my name and say, 'I am he,' and 'The time has arrived.' Do not go after them.
When you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified, for this must happen first, and the end will not come immediately.
Then he said to them: "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;
And there will be very great earthquakes from place to place, famines and plagues, terrors from heaven, and there will be very great signs.
But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you and hand you over to synagogues and prison, and they will bring you before kings and rulers for the sake of my name.
And this will turn out for you as a testimony.
"Settle it in your hearts not to rehearse beforehand what answer you will give,"
For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which none of your adversaries will be able to resist or answer.
For you will be handed over by parents and brothers and friends and relatives, and they will put some of you to death;
And you will be hated by all for my name's sake.
And not a hair of your head will perish.
And by your endurance you will gain your souls.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by a host, then understand that its desolation has drawn near.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let those who are inside it escape; and let those who are out in the countryside not enter there.
For these are the days of its vengeance, that all that is written may be fulfilled.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing in those days, for then there will be great distress upon the earth and wrath upon this people.
And they will fall by the edge of the sword and be carried off captive by all the Gentiles; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
And there will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth anguish of the nations, in bewilderment and groaning, as from the sea and its tumult;
with the spirits of men [?] from fear and expectation of what is coming upon this world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming on a cloud with power and great glory.
And when all this begins to take place, lift up your eyes and raise your heads, for your redemption has drawn near.
And he told them a parable: Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they put forth leaves, you know for yourselves that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all this taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away until all this takes place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
Take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with indulgence and drunkenness and the cares of this world, and that day come upon you suddenly.
For like a snare it will come upon those who dwell on the face of all the earth.
Watch, therefore, at all times and pray, that you may be found worthy to escape all this that is going to take place, and to stand before the Son of Man.
And he himself was in the temple by day and taught; but at night he would go out and stay on the mount called the Mount of Olives.
And all the people rose early to come to him in the temple to hear his words.
The feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was drawing near.
And the chief priests and the scribes sought him, how they might kill him, but they feared the people.
And the devil entered into Judas, who was called Iscariot, and he was of the number of the twelve.
And he went and conferred with the chief priests and the scribes and the leaders of the people, how he might hand him over to them.
They were glad and promised to give him silver.
He agreed with them, and he looked for a good time to hand him over to them away from the crowd.
The days of Unleavened Bread came, when the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
He sent Peter and John and said to them: "Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat it."
They said to him: "Where do you want us to prepare it for you?"
And he himself said to them: Behold, as soon as you enter the city, a man will meet you carrying a jar of water; follow him to the house, wherever he enters,
and say to the master of the house: The Teacher says to you: Where is the lodging in which I may eat this Passover with my disciples?
He will show you a large upper room, already furnished. Make it ready for us there."
And they went and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, he sat down at the table, and the twelve apostles with him.
And he said to them: With earnest desire my heart has longed to eat this Passover with you before my suffering.
For I tell you: I will not eat of it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
And he took the cup, gave thanks, and said: "Take this and divide it among yourselves."
But I say to you: from now on I will drink no more of the fruit of this vine until the kingdom of God comes.
And he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them and said: This is my body, given for you; do this in remembrance of me, --
likewise the cup -- after supper, and he said: This cup -- the new covenant of my blood, poured out for you.
But look, the hand of the one who betrays me is with me on the table.
The Son of Man indeed goes according to what has been decreed for him, but woe to that man by whom he is handed over!
They began to ask one another which of them it could be who was going to do this.
And there was also a dispute among them as to which of them was the greatest.
But he himself said to them: The kings of the gentiles lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called benefactors.
But you shall not be so; rather, let the greatest among you be as the youngest, and the leader as a servant.
Who is greater: the one who reclines at table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines at table? But I am among you as a servant.
And you are the ones who have stood by me in my trials.
"And I promise you, just as my Father promised me, a kingdom,"
So that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and you shall sit on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
"Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to have you, to sift you like wheat."
But I have besought my Father for you, that your faith may not fail you, and when at some time you turn back, strengthen your brothers.
But he said: Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death.
But he himself said: I tell you, Peter, the cock will not crow today until you have denied me three times, saying that you do not know me.
And he said to them: When I sent you out without purse and bag and sandals, did you lack anything? And they said: We lacked nothing.
And then he said: But now, let whoever has a money pouch take it, and likewise a bag as well; and let whoever has none sell his garment and buy a sword.
I tell you: this scripture alone must yet be fulfilled in me, namely: He was counted among the lawless; for what concerns me has an end.
But they said to him: Lord, behold, here are two daggers. And he himself said to them: It is enough.
And he came out from there and went, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples also followed him.
And when he came to the place, he said to them: Pray, that you may not enter into temptation.
And he himself withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and knelt down, and prayed,
and said: Father, if you are willing that this cup pass from me — yet not my will, but let your will be done!
And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
And being in agony, he prayed all the more. And his sweat became like drops of blood falling down upon the earth.
And he rose from prayer and came to his disciples and found them sleeping from sorrow
And he said to them: "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation."

And while he was still saying this, behold, a crowd, and the one called Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, was leading them, and he came near to Jesus to kiss him, for he had given them this sign, saying: The one I kiss is he.
But Jesus said to him: Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?
When those who were with him saw this thing, they said to him: Lord, if you wish, let us slay these men with the sword.
And a certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
Jesus answered and said to them, "Let it go this far!" And he touched his ear and healed him.
And Jesus said to the chief priests and the captains of the temple and the elders who had come against him: You have come out with swords and clubs, as against a robber.
Day after day I was with you in the temple, and you did not stretch out your hand against me; but this is your hour and the power of darkness.
And when they had seized him, they led him away and brought him into the house of the high priest, and Peter followed from afar.
And they kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down around it; Peter too sat down among them.
And a certain maidservant saw him sitting in the light, and she looked at him closely and said: This man too was with him.
But he denied it and said, "Woman, I do not know him."
And a little later another saw him and said: You also are one of them. But Peter said: Man, I am not one of them.
About an hour later someone else insisted, saying, "This man was certainly with him too, for he is a Galilean."
But Peter said to him: Man, I do not know what you are saying. And immediately, while he was still saying this, the rooster crowed.
And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, which he had said to him: Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times, saying that you do not know me.
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
But the men who had seized Jesus were mocking him and beating him,
and they covered his head and were striking him, and they questioned him, saying: Prophesy, who is it that struck you?
And they reviled him with many other blasphemies and spoke them to him.
And when day broke, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes gathered, and they brought him up to their council
and said to him: If you are the Christ, tell us! Jesus said to them: If I tell you, you will not believe me;
and if I question you, you will not answer me anything, nor release me.
From now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
And they all said to him: Are you then the Son of God? And Jesus said to them: You say that I am.
And they said: What further testimony do we need? We ourselves have heard it from his own mouth.
And their whole multitude arose and brought him to Pilate.
And they began to accuse him, saying: We found this man subverting our nation and forbidding the giving of tribute to Caesar, and saying that he himself is the Christ and a king.
Pilate questioned him and said to him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" He said to him, "You say so."
But Pilate said to the chief priests and to all the people: I find no guilt in this man.
But they grew all the more insistent and said, "He stirs up the people and teaches throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place."
But when Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked them whether this man was a Galilean.
And he understood that he was from the jurisdiction of Herod; he sent him to Herod, for he too was in Jerusalem at that time, during these days.
But when Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had been hearing about him, and he desired to see some miracle done by him.
And he questioned him at length, but he himself gave him no answer at all.
The chief priests and the scribes stood and earnestly accused him.
But Herod treated him with contempt, and his people also, and they mocked him and clothed him in a shining garment. And he sent him back to Pilate.
And Pilate and Herod became friends with each other on that day, for before this they had been enemies.
But Pilate summoned the chief priests and the rulers and the people
and said to them: You brought me this man as one who subverts the people, and I examined him before you and found nothing in this man of what you accuse him of,
and neither did Herod, for I sent him to him; and he has done nothing deserving death.
I will therefore punish him and release him."
For he was obliged to release one man to them at the feast.
The whole multitude cried out, saying: Take that man away and release Barabbas to us,
who had been thrown into prison for causing a riot in the city and for murder.
Again Pilate called to them, for he wanted to release Jesus.
But they shouted and said: Crucify him!
And he said to them a third time: What evil has this man done? I have found no guilt worthy of death in him; I will discipline him and release him.
But they pressed on with a loud voice and demanded that he be crucified, and their voices and those of the chief priests prevailed.
Then Pilate decided that their demand should be granted,
And he released to them Barabbas, who had been thrown into prison for sedition and murder, the one they were demanding, but Jesus he handed over to their will.
And as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the field, and laid the cross on him, and he carried it behind Jesus.
And a multitude of the people followed him, and of women, who were beating themselves and lamenting him.
Jesus turned to them and said: Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over me, but weep for yourselves and for your children,
for days are coming in which they will say: Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not give birth, and the breasts that did not nurse!
Then they will begin to say to the mountains: Fall on us! and to the hills: Cover us!
If they do this to the green tree, what will happen to the dry one?
They also brought two others, evildoers, to be put to death with him.
And when they came to the place called the Place of the Skull, there they crucified him and those evildoers, one on his right and the other on his left.
But Jesus said: Forgive them, Father, for they do not know what they are doing. -- And they divided his garments and cast lots.
And the people stood and watched, and the rulers with them also mocked him and said: He saved others; let him save himself too, if he is the Christ, the chosen one of God.
The soldiers also ridiculed him, coming up to him and offering him vinegar
and saying to him: If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!
There was also an inscription written over him in Greek, Roman, and Hebrew letters, saying that this is the King of the Jews.
But one of the evildoers who had been hanged blasphemed him and said to him: If you are the Christ, save yourself and us as well.
The other companion answered, rebuked him and said to him, "Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
For we are justly receiving what is due for what we have done, but this man has done nothing lawless.
And he said to Jesus: Remember me when you come in your kingdom.
And Jesus said to him, "Amen, I say to you: today you will be with me in Paradise."
And it was the sixth hour, and there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
The sun was darkened, and the curtain of the temple was torn down the middle.
And Jesus called out with a loud voice and said: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit. -- And he gave up his spirit.
And when the centurion saw this event, he glorified God and said: Truly this man was righteous.
And all who had come with them, and who saw this sight and this event, beat their breasts and went away.
And all his acquaintances stood at a distance. And the women who had followed him from Galilee watched this.
And behold, a man named Joseph, a councillor, was a good and righteous man.
This man had not been party to their counsel and their deed. He was from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, and he too was waiting for the kingdom of God.
This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
And he took him down and wrapped him in a linen shroud and laid him in a tomb hewn out of rock, where no one had yet been laid.
And that day was Friday, and the Sabbath was dawning.
The women also, who had come with him from Galilee, followed after, and they saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
And they went away and prepared spices and ointment; and on that Sabbath they rested, according to the commandment.
But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared, and certain others were with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
When they went inside, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
And while they were perplexed about this, behold, two men in shining garments stood over them.
And as they were frightened and bowed their faces to the ground, the men said to them: "Why do you seek the living one among the dead?
He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee.
And he said: The Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men and be crucified, and on the third day rise.
And they remembered his words.
And they returned and told these words to the eleven and to all the others.
Now they were Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the mother of James, and certain others with them, who were telling this to the apostles.
And their words seemed to them like foolishness, and they did not believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb, and he looked in and saw only the linen cloths lying there, and he went away by himself, marveling at this matter.
And behold, two of them were going that same day to a village named Emmaus, which is one hundred and sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem.
And they were talking with one another about all that had happened.
And it happened that as they were talking and inquiring, Jesus himself drew near to them and walked along with them.
But their eyes were held, so that they could not recognize him.
And he said to them: What are these words that you are disputing with one another as you walk, and why are you sorrowful?
One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said to him: Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who does not know what has happened in it in these days?
And he said to them: What things? And they said to him: Concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet, mighty in his deeds and his word before God and the people;
how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to the judgment of death and crucified him.
But we were hoping that he was the one who would redeem Israel; and besides all this, this is now the third day since this happened.
Moreover, certain women of ours astonished us, for they went at dawn to the tomb
and did not find his body. They came and said that they had even seen a vision of angels, who told them that he is alive.
And some of us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see.
And he said to them: O you ignorant ones, slow of heart to believe all that the prophets spoke!
Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer in this way and enter into his glory?
And beginning from Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
And they drew near to the village to which they were going, but he himself made as though to go on farther.
They pressed him and said to him: Stay with us, for it is evening, and the day has declined. And he went in to stay with them.
And it happened, as he sat at table with them, that he took bread, blessed it, and broke it and gave it to them.
Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him. And he vanished from their sight.
And they said to one another: Was not our heart burning within us as he spoke to us on the road and as he interpreted the scriptures to us?
And they rose up that same hour and returned to Jerusalem, and they found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
And they said: Truly the Lord has risen and has appeared to Simon.
And they recounted what had happened on the road and how he was revealed to them in the breaking of the bread.
And just as they were saying this, Jesus himself stood among them and said to them: Peace be with you! It is I, do not be afraid!
But they trembled and became frightened; they thought that they were seeing some spirit.
And he said to them: Why are you troubled, and why do many thoughts come into your hearts?
See my hands and feet, for it is I myself. Touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.
And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
And while they still did not believe, because of their joy and wonder, Jesus said to them: Do you have any food here?
And they held out to him a piece of broiled fish, a half, and a honeycomb.
And he ate in their presence, and took what was left and gave it to them,
And he said to them: These are the words that I spoke to you while I was with you, that everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms must be fulfilled.
Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,
and he said to them: Thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day.
and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations. Begin from Jerusalem,
for you are witnesses of all these things.
And behold, I will send you the promise of my Father. But you, stay in this city, Jerusalem, until you are clothed with power from on high.
And he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifted up his hands and blessed them.
And it happened, as Jesus was blessing them, that he parted from them and went up into heaven.
And they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they were continually in the temple and blessed God.
